title: Same Alarm
tone: deadpan, then quiet, then deadpan again
logline: A man gives a day everything it asks for and discovers it was asking for nothing.

spine.want: to get through the day without being noticed
spine.obstacle: every day is the same day, so getting through it costs him nothing and buys him nothing
spine.turn: the room empties and nothing is asked of him — the first thing the day has ever given him
spine.button: the alarm goes again, and for the first time he leaves it ringing

narration.text: Same alarm, same six, same ceiling he has stared at for a decade, and the same corridor behind a door.
Nine hours under a light that never changes, someone needs it sooner than yesterday, and he says yes because he is good.
He is good at yes, good at sooner, good at the voice that says it will only take a single minute.
Then the room empties and nobody needs anything, he stays, the light does not, and at six the alarm goes again.
This time he does not reach for it, because the hand that always rises is still, and the ceiling keeps its question.
The corridor is the same corridor, the doors are the same doors, and the clock has not moved all morning.
He counts the tiles to the lift, the lift counts floors, and the numbers arrive at the same office with the window.
Somebody calls his name down the corridor, and he turns before he has decided to, because that is what the day is.
At six the alarm goes again, the hand rises, and the ceiling keeps the question for tomorrow, as always.
